correctness.rationale: Quantifier elimination reduces complete 1-types to equality congruences on unary terms. Finite generated quotients have finite transition-table isolating formulas. Infinite quotients cannot be isolated because every finite term diagram has a finite completion. Every finite diagram inside an infinite quotient also has at least two distinct infinite completions by opening one unresolved transition to an infinite ray and changing a later F-transition. Hence the first derivative is exactly the infinite-orbit locus and is perfect; compact metrizability and zero-dimensionality identify it with Cantor space.

value.rationale: The theorem converts a known non-smallness/cardinality result into an exact Stone-space decomposition. It identifies the natural finite/infinite generated-orbit boundary, shows the isolated types are dense, and locates all perfect behavior in one Cantor kernel. This is a structurally meaningful invariant and a sharp contrast with the scattered one-unary-function case.
